channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: How to Read a Full P&ID: A Complete Worked Walkthrough
item.description: A complete, start-to-finish walkthrough of reading a P&ID — equipment and line symbols, tag anatomy, valve types, a fully worked example tracing a real control loop end to end, common misreads, and revision/document-control basics.

item.title: P&ID Instrument Bubbles: Line Types & Tag Anatomy Explained
item.description: What the line under an instrument bubble means — field-mounted, control-room-mounted, or inaccessible — plus how to break down a tag like TT01 using ISA S5.1.

item.title: Legend Sheet in a P&ID Explained
item.description: A legend sheet is the reference table that defines every symbol, line type and tag format on a P&ID — why everyone reads the same drawing the same way.

item.title: P&ID (Piping & Instrumentation Diagram) Explained
item.description: How to actually read a P&ID — equipment, piping, valves, instrumentation tags, and signal lines — plus ISA tag-naming logic and how a P&ID differs from a PFD.

item.title: 33/11 kV Substation: Single Line Diagram & Equipment Overview
item.description: How a 33/11 kV substation is built, walked through its single line diagram from incoming line to distribution feeders — every equipment item and its function.

item.title: Main Components of a 33 kV Substation Explained
item.description: Every stage of a 33 kV substation feeding a 0.433 kV LT network — incoming supply, HT switchgear, busbar, transformer feeder, power transformer, LT panel and outgoing distribution — plus earthing and auxiliary systems.

item.title: 4-20mA Current Loops: Why Industry Still Trusts an Analog Signal
item.description: Why 4-20mA beat 0-20mA and voltage signals for instrumentation, what live-zero actually protects against, how to convert a reading back to engineering units.

item.title: Essential Protection Settings of Air Circuit Breakers (ACB) Explained
item.description: LTPU, LTD, STPU, STD, instantaneous and ground fault settings on an ACB — what each does, typical ranges, and why they exist as a coordinated set.

item.title: Access Control System (ACS) Explained: Components, Architecture & Site Work
item.description: How an Access Control System actually works — main components, the six-step credential-to-unlock sequence, architecture, and integration with FAS/BMS/CCTV.

item.title: AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU, CSAHU: What Is the Difference?
item.description: What separates an AHU, FAHU, FCU, FMAHU and CSAHU — air source, installation style and typical application for each, in one comparison.

item.title: Air Changes per Hour: What ACH Actually Tells You (and Doesn't)
item.description: What air changes per hour (ACH) measures, the formula behind it, typical ACH targets by space type.

item.title: Alarm Setpoint Bands: Why High and High-High Are Different Alarms
item.description: Why alarms come in High/High-High and Low/Low-Low pairs, not single trip points, and how a reset deadband on each keeps the alarm list from flooding operators.

item.title: ANSI Relay Numbers: Common Protection Relay Functions
item.description: A working reference for the ANSI device numbers you'll actually run into on protection schemes — 50/51, 27/59, 87, 21, 67, 25 and more.

item.title: ATS, MTS, ECB & Switch Disconnectors: Transfer & Isolation Switching Devices Explained
item.description: ATS, MTS, COS, switch disconnectors, load break switches, fused switch disconnectors and ECBs — what each device does, how it differs, and where it's used.

item.title: Basics of Fire Protection in Buildings Explained
item.description: Passive protection, active systems, detection, suppression and evacuation — the five layers of building fire protection and how they work together.

item.title: Battery SoC vs DoD: Why They're Not the Same Number
item.description: Why SoC and DoD are two views of the same battery, how SoC is actually estimated in the field, and why chemistry sets the DoD limit that protects cycle life.

item.title: Beam Bending Basics: Why Section Modulus Decides Capacity, Not Just Load
item.description: Why a beam's bending capacity comes down to two checks — bending stress against section modulus, and deflection against span — not just the applied load.

item.title: Bearing Failures: Root Causes & Prevention
item.description: The five most common ways rolling-element bearings actually fail — spalling, lubrication breakdown, contamination, electrical erosion, and false brinelling.

item.title: Belt Drive Sizing: Why the Speed Ratio Alone Doesn't Tell You the Tension
item.description: Belt drive speed ratio, belt velocity and shaft torque from pulley diameters and power, and why tension depends on wrap angle and friction, not just geometry.

item.title: BMS Point Types Explained: AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV, MV
item.description: What each BMS point abbreviation actually means — AI, AO, BI, BO, MI, MO, BV, AV and MV.

item.title: BOD & BOP in Pipe Bending: The Key to Piping Take-Off & Fabrication
item.description: BOD (Bend Outside Diameter) and BOP (Bend Center Line) drive piping take-off and fabrication. Formulas, a bend allowance table, and a worked 90° bend example.

item.title: Bolt Torque vs Preload: Why K-Factor Is the Number That Actually Matters
item.description: Bolt tightening torque from target preload using the short-form torque-tension relationship, and why the nut factor dominates the result more than bolt grade.

item.title: Breaker Selectivity: Why Two Correctly Rated Breakers Can Still Trip Together
item.description: What selectivity (discrimination) between breakers actually means, the Ir < Isd < Ii hierarchy behind it.

item.title: Busbar Sizing: Why the Short-Circuit Check Often Governs, Not the Continuous Rating
item.description: Busbar cross-section from continuous current rating, then checked against short-circuit thermal withstand and electrodynamic force.

item.title: Cable Glands: What They Do and How to Get the Selection Right
item.description: What a cable gland is actually holding together, the main gland types and their parts, a selection and quality-inspection checklist.

item.title: Cable Size & Current Capacity: A Practical Selection Guide
item.description: Approximate current-carrying capacity for copper and aluminium cables by cross-section, common house-wiring cable sizes by load.

item.title: Cable Tray vs Cable Ladder vs Cable Trunking vs Conduit
item.description: Cable tray, cable ladder, cable trunking, and conduit compared — construction, protection level, typical load, where each is used, and how to choose between them.

item.title: CAV vs VAV: Constant vs Variable Air Volume Explained
item.description: CAV and VAV compared — how each airflow control strategy works, key features, pros and cons, and which building types each one actually suits.

item.title: Cavitation vs. Flashing in Control Valves: What's the Difference?
item.description: Cavitation and flashing both start with the same vapor-pressure event in a control valve — downstream is what makes one loud and pitted, the other eroded.

item.title: Centrifugal Pump Components Explained
item.description: What every part of a centrifugal pump actually does — impeller, volute casing, shaft, seal, bearings, and coupling — component by component.
